question: Where does a held block sit, and does the window width decide the center line on phones?
how: real mouse in headless Chrome on an empty not-linked page, with one new blank section and new Shape blocks, nothing saved: Exit Without Saving after each run. Desktop frame 1600 wide, row pitch 41.09, column pitch 58.79. Phone frame 428 wide, 10 tracks, column pitch 48.45. bx and by are the block's distance from where it started.
start: a press does nothing. A move past 10px starts the drag but changes nothing: no ring, no transform. The next move shows it. A release right after that one move is no drag: one move of 200, 100 and a release left the area as it was.
follows: inside the limits the block is at the pointer on both axes, moving down, up, left and right, and at the same place coming back. Holding still changes nothing (1.5s waits).

limits.top: the top of the grid box
limits.bottom: the bottom of the grid box, which grows with the target in the same move: bottom gap 0
limits.left: the left of the grid box, within 0.33px
limits.right: 4px short of the grid box: the block's right edge stops at 1596 of 1600 and at 423.67 of 428. Why 4 is not known, it is what both views measure
limits.target: the limits hold the block only. The target and the ring still follow the pointer

grid: the grid has max(its own rows, last row of the target) rows while held, going down and coming back up: 8 rows, 11 at target 6 / 2 / 12 / 8, 13 at 8 / 2 / 14 / 8, 9 at 4 / 2 / 10 / 8, 8 at 1 / 2 / 7 / 8
width: a lone held block has the width of its target. It takes a margin track when the target does: 341.75 becomes 382.95 at 1 / 21 / 7 / 27 and at 1 / 1 / 7 / 7. Wider, its left edge stays where it was. Narrower, its center stays where it was: from 1 / 1 / 7 / 7 at dx 80 the block is at 100.55 and not 80. A group keeps its widths. Measured again with a press near the left of a block: the place pressed stays under the pointer, so narrower moves the block by the share pressed. From 1 / 21 / 7 / 27 pressed 30 from its left the block moves by 3.12 of the 41.28 it loses; pressed at the middle, by 20.55. A center press looks like keeping the center.
target: the step rule is G4's, in SNAP.json. These sweeps agree with it: sideways it stays to dx 34 and moves at 35, then at 94; coming back the same; down it stays to 26 and moves at 27, then at 68. Full width 1 / 2 / 7 / 26 stays to dx 50 and goes to 1 / 3 / 7 / 27 at dx 60; on phones full width goes between dx 12 and 16 on both sides. The limits below do not stop the target. One exception to the edge in front, from one sweep: a block on the left margin track going right goes by its left edge: 1 / 1 / 7 / 7 stays at dx 40, 1 / 2 / 7 / 8 at dx 80 and 120, 1 / 19 / 7 / 25 at dx 1100.
group: All blocks move together, and the top, left and bottom of the group's box stop at the grid: top and left at its side (pressed block anywhere in the group), the bottom at the bottom of the grid, inferred from two groups of two heights. On the right each block stops by itself, where it would be 4px short of the grid if it stood at the box's left: left block at 1 / 1 / 7 / 7, right block at 1 / 15 / 7 / 21, widths 382.95 and 341.75, the left one stops at tx 1213.04, the right one at tx 1254.25, whichever is pressed. So they can part by the difference, and a block further right goes far outside the grid (2460). Widths stay on desktop. On a phone the block also gets a lone block's shift when its target is narrower (-30: tx -18.81, 20: tx 22 at the limit); on desktop a group from the margin track gets none (300: tx 300). Rings: the same limits as a lone block, on the box. A group's line on phones goes by where the box is, yellow within half a column of center; on desktop an odd-width group stays dashed (GUIDES.json).

centerLine.window: the window width does not decide it. Mobile View holds at windows 1600, 1000, 800 and 500 (a window asked to be 428 came out 500) gave the same 17 readings: the frame is 428 wide in all of them
centerLine.phones: phones have the line, in the same place and colors, but only while it is yellow: no dashed line, at any point in 3 sweeps. The earlier single hold at a 428 window was away from the center
centerLine.rule: a lone held block: yellow when the center of the block at its own width is within half a column of the canvas center, on desktop and on phones. Not the target: full width stays on the centered target 1 / 2 / 7 / 26 to dx 50, but is dashed from dx 30, and on phones 1 / 3 / 7 / 11 is yellow to 23.67 off the center. A resize goes by the target: east -24 yellow at 1 / 2 / 7 / 10, east -36 none at 1 / 2 / 7 / 9.
centerLine.snap: phones also center-snap: a 7 column block takes one more column within half a column of the center, as 1 / 2 / 7 / 10, at width 376

notMeasured: A group's bottom limit where the blocks reach it with the grid at its own height. Why the right limit is 4px. Whether the group narrowing is a phone rule or some other rule: only those cases. Group resize's start move: not measured, ours starts on the press (GROUPRESIZE.json).

knownMisses.why: the center is 0.1px outside half a column on the oracle and just inside on ours: 376 and 376.66 wide

knownMisses.sweep: from the margin track, far right
knownMisses.why: the last step comes later on the oracle: to 1 / 20 / 7 / 26 between 1160 and 1170, ours at 1135. No rule found: one sweep, the steps before fit

in its first 90px left a block from the right margin lands where no rule says: -5 to -45 at 1 / 18 / 7 / 24, -50 to -90 at 1 / 19 / 7 / 25, also on a drop; from -100 the step rule fits. Ours follows the rule. Seen on two runs and five drops

knownMisses.sweep: resize w to the far side
knownMisses.why: 0.05px from the step: the pointer was on the block's edge, ours is on the center of the handle

marginTrack.left: a box that starts on the left margin track goes as far as the last column: 1 / 20 / 7 / 26 for a block six wide, never 21 / 27, also a group: 1 / 9 / 7 / 26 and 1 / 6 / 7 / 26
marginTrack.right: a block from the right margin goes on to the left margin: 1 / 1 / 7 / 7 at dx -1170
marginTrack.pressMiss: the section toolbar lies over the right of a section: a press there is not a press on the block
marginTrack.otherWidths: the first steps from the right margin differ by width: four wide from 1 / 23 / 7 / 27 stays to -50 and is at 22 / 26 from -70, 21 / 25 at -160, 20 / 24 at -200. Six wide: see knownMisses. No rule fits both

resize.start: the same as a drag: the move past 10px changes nothing, the next one shows the ring
resize.follows: the block's own box follows the pointer on the sides held, in pixels, and only the ring snaps. East: wider by dx, x stays. West: x moves by dx by transform, wider by -dx. South: taller by dy. North: y moves by dy by transform, taller by -dy. Its grid area stays until the release
resize.least: one column wide (47.78) and one row high (30.09). A text block is as high as the rows its content needs: 194.47 for five rows, also while the pointer goes on
resize.limits: the sides of the grid box, with no 4px: right 1600.13, left 0.13, top the top of the grid, bottom the bottom, which grows and shrinks with the ring
resize.centerLine: goes by the target, not the box: yellow at 1 / 2 / 7 / 26
resize.textWidth: the ring takes the rows the text needs. On the oracle these lag one move behind the box's width (-300: ring 1 / 2 / 8 / 5 with 448 content, the rows of the width before); ours reads the width now
resize.dropNotHeld: after a drop that widens a text block the rows fall to what the text needs: 1 / 2 / 42 / 8 held dropped at 1 / 2 / 6 / 8 with 202 content, belongs to X8
